s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive extraocular muscle limitation with a localized orbital mass
salient_findings: Slowly developing limitation in right-eye movement
Restricted abduction of the right eye
Extraconal mass at the right superolateral orbital wall with smooth bone remodeling
key_facts: 5-year-old boy with no prior medical history
No pain, inflammation, fever, trauma, or history of ocular infection
Overall health unchanged
Abduction of the right eye was restricted
No signs of proptosis, strabismus, visual impairment, or inflammation in either eye
Laboratory studies, including an infectious work-up, were negative
Noncontrast CT showed a well-circumscribed extraconal mass at the right superolateral orbital wall
MRI demonstrated a cystic mass in the right superior extraconal compartment
Mild compression on the external and superior rectus muscles
No involvement of the optic nerve, intraconal fat, or intracranial extension

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass with smooth bone remodeling and fluid-attenuating content on imaging

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass with hyperintense signal on T2-weighted images and no internal enhancement

shortlist.label: Orbital lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass with mild compression on surrounding muscles and no involvement of optic nerve or intraconal fat

shortlist.label: Colloid cyst of the orbit
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass with fluid-attenuating content and no bone invasion

shortlist.label: Orbital enterogenous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass with smooth bone remodeling and no signs of inflammation or infection

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-circumscribed extraconal mass with smooth bone remodeling and fluid-attenuating content on CT, along with the cystic appearance on MRI that is hyperintense on T2-weighted images and hypointense on FLAIR imaging, is consistent with a dermoid cyst. The lack of enhancement after gadolinium administration and the absence of aggressive features such as bone invasion also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: While similar to dermoid cysts, epidermoid cysts are less common in the orbit and typically do not contain the same variety of tissue elements.

rejected.label: Orbital lymphangioma
rejected.why: Lymphangiomas are more likely to have a complex, multicystic appearance and may show enhancement after gadolinium administration due to their vascular nature.

rejected.label: Colloid cyst of the orbit
rejected.why: Colloid cysts are rare in the orbit and typically have a more solid appearance on imaging, with possible calcification and contrast enhancement.

rejected.label: Orbital enterogenous cyst
rejected.why: Enterogenous cysts are rare and usually present with more pronounced clinical symptoms due to their potential for infection or rupture, which is not seen in this case.
